title: The board as a pane beside the agent's terminal

decision.q: The board in the pane tree

options.label: Yes: a board pane you can split beside any terminal
options.act: PaneLeaf.ref → enum { command(CommandRef), review(scope) }; ⌘⇧↩ maximises it
options.then: Let a pane hold the board as well as a terminal, so it splits beside the agent's terminal.

options.label: No: The board is a separate tab of the project window

why: Switchboard's windows are a tree of split panes, and each leaf holds one terminal (PaneLeaf.ref: CommandRef?). Let a leaf hold the board instead. Then Claude's terminal and its the board sit side by side: you answer on the right and watch the agent pick it up on the left. ⌘⇧↩ already maximises a pane, which is the zone with no new window at all.
Xcode's assistant editor and tmux work this way. The change is small: the leaf's ref becomes "a command or the board".
